title: PracticePay Patient Financing Reset Payment: Balance, Payments, Rate and Rounding
content:
A reset of a PracticePay Patient Financing plan sets a new monthly payment from the figures below.

## 1. Due dates

The plan's first due date is the first date on its due day at least 25 calendar days after the purchase date, and the remaining payments are the due dates from the plan's next due date through its final due date, the final due date falling the term less one whole months after the first due date, so that the remaining payments are the term less the whole months from the first due date to the next due date, never fewer than one. The due dates on or before a date are those from the first due date through that date.

## 2. Reset balance and reset payments

The reset balance is the plan balance, fees owed included, less the plan's amount past due, which stays due as it stands; the reset payments are the remaining payments when the plan has no amount past due and, when it has one, the due dates after the latest due date before today, every installment due before today staying in the amount past due and an installment due today counting among the reset payments, never fewer than one, and the reset payment applies from the first due date among them.

## 3. Rate and payment

The reset rate is the plan APR. The reset payment is the level payment that repays the reset balance at the reset rate over the reset payments (the monthly rate being the reset rate divided by 1200), or the reset balance divided equally over the reset payments when the reset rate is 0, rounded up to the next cent and never below the plan's smallest monthly payment.

Stated generally for every reset: every rate cut is subtracted from the plan APR, never below 0, to give the reset rate; under every way of working out the payment, the payment is that way's interest-free part divided equally over that way's payments plus the level payment that repays the rest of the reset balance at the reset rate over those payments, or the rest divided equally over them when the reset rate is 0, worked out once at the reset rate, rounded up to the next cent and never below the plan's smallest monthly payment; and the reset rate is stored as the plan APR from the reset onward. In the payment of the paragraph above there is no interest-free part and the payments are the reset payments. Every reset payment method repays the reset balance with exactly the reset payments, the last reset payment taking only the rounding difference.

## 4. When a reset is made

A reset payment is never below the plan's smallest monthly payment, so a reset that is made always sets a payment and never a payment of 0.00; when no reset is made the reset payment is 0.00 and nothing is written, and a reset that would leave both the monthly payment and the plan APR as they are makes no change and is not made.

A plan whose deferred interest was billed is reset under this schedule only once, only while no payment dated on or after the billing date has posted on it, and only before the first due date after the billing; a plan already reset, which is a plan whose monthly payment no longer equals the level payment its payment method set at activation, rounded up to the next cent and never below the plan's smallest monthly payment, or whose plan APR no longer equals the plan APR of its plan, or a plan past either point is not reset, and its monthly payment and plan APR stay as they are.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

A plan with a plan balance of 1300.00 USD, of which 100.00 USD is past due; 12 due dates remain after the latest due date before today; an APR taken as 12.00 for illustration, so a monthly rate of 0.01.

- Reset balance: 1300.00 less 100.00, that is 1200.00; the 100.00 stays past due.
- Level payment: 1200.00 repaid at 0.01 a month over 12 payments is 106.6185…, rounded up to 106.62 USD.
- At a rate of 0 the same balance would be 1200.00 divided by 12, that is 100.00 USD.

*Deferred-interest timing (hypothetical).* Billing date 10 September, first due date after it 1 October: a payment dated 10 September bars the reset; with no payment since, a reset asked for on 30 September can be made, and one asked for on 1 October cannot.
